Reporting a full outage of the Finance shared drive (F:\Finance) as of 9:12 AM. Symptom: all mapped drive connections return 'network path not found' across every workstation in the Finance and Accounting departments, roughly 40 users total. I confirmed this is not a local issue by testing from three separate machines on two different switches; both fail identically, and ping to the file server (10.20.4.15) times out. The server's status light is amber and the console appears unresponsive to RDP. This is blocking the entire team's ability to work: payroll processing is due to run at noon today and pulls source files directly from this share, invoicing cannot close month-end without the drive, and several finance staff are currently sitting idle waiting on access. I attempted a manual reboot of the file server via the rack KVM at 9:20 AM with no change in status. This needs escalation to on-call infrastructure immediately, as we are now roughly two and a half hours from the payroll cutoff and have no workaround; running payroll from local cached copies is not an option since several files were mid-edit when the server dropped. Please treat this as a P1 and let me know who is engaging so I can coordinate testing from this end once the server is back.

I ran the standard diagnostic suite (ipconfig /all, ping sweep to the gateway, traceroute to the internal DNS servers) and everything downstream of the router resolves normally; latency to the core switch sits around 4ms, well within spec. For what it's worth, I sat in on the infrastructure retro yesterday and the team walked through the planned firmware rollout for the AP fleet next quarter, which looks reasonable, though I'd push for a staged rollout rather than all-at-once given past regressions.

Relevant to my actual situation: my connection to the office Wi-Fi has been dropping roughly every twenty minutes since Tuesday, only at my desk, confirmed by moving two rows over and having it hold steady there. That said, and I promise this is not simply my own aesthetic complaint dressed up as something bigger: earlier this afternoon I discovered that an email had gone out from my account to the entire company distribution list, all four hundred or so of us, impersonating our chief financial officer and requesting that recipients click a link to 'verify' a wire transfer authorization. I did not send it. I have not clicked anything unusual myself in recent memory, though I suppose I cannot rule it out entirely. Several colleagues have already replied-all asking whether it is legitimate, which of course only spreads it further through everyone's inbox as we speak.

I also wanted to mention, purely for completeness and not because it matters much right now, that my own email signature still has the old office address on it from before we moved buildings last spring, and the logo image seems to render a touch blurry on some screens, though that has been the case for months and has never once affected anyone's ability to read what I send.

In any case, the distribution list matter above seems like the one that actually needs looking at without delay, given how many people it has already reached and how quickly it is spreading.
